roles.title: General Secretary - (Multiple Regions Available)
description: Behind every high-functioning team is someone who keeps everything moving: the meetings organised, the actions followed up, the information flowing to the right people at the right time. That person is the General Secretary.

As GenSec for FOSIS Midlands, you will work closely with the Midlands Chair to keep the regional team running smoothly. This is operational, detail-oriented work, and it matters. The programmes FOSIS delivers, the events that bring students together, the campaigns that represent Muslim students to the country - all of it depends on a team that is well-coordinated and well-supported. That is what you will make possible.
What You'll Be Doing

Administration & Organisation: Keep the Midlands team's operations in good order. Maintain documents, track project progress, manage timelines, and make sure the right information reaches the right people.
Meetings & Coordination: Organise and schedule team meetings, prepare agendas with the Chair, take accurate minutes, and follow up on actions so nothing falls through the cracks.
Internal Communications: Support the flow of information across the team. Keep communication channels clear, contact lists updated, and team members informed on priorities and updates.
Team Support: Be the operational backbone for events, campaigns, and projects. Support team members with what they need to deliver their work effectively.
Strategic Support: Work with the Midlands Chair to track progress against regional objectives and contribute ideas that help the team operate better.
What We're Looking For

You are organised, dependable, and calm under pressure. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, manage multiple deadlines without losing the thread, and find genuine satisfaction in making a team work well. Experience with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, or project management tools is a bonus, but what matters most is reliability and a collaborative mindset.
What You'll Gain

Hands-on experience in administration, coordination, and operational leadership within a national student organisation. You will develop skills in project management, communications, and team coordination, and play a direct role in making Muslim student life across the Midlands better.

This is a voluntary role designed to fit around your studies. The GenSec is expected to maintain regular communication with the team, attend meetings, and support the effective running of FOSIS Midlands throughout the academic year.

roles.title: ISoc Mentor
description: Muslim students across the Midlands are doing incredible things: building communities, navigating university life, and trying to hold on to their deen while the world pulls in every direction. Your job is to make sure FOSIS is standing with them.

As an ISoc Representative, you are the bridge between FOSIS and the Islamic Societies in your region. You will build real relationships with ISoc committees, carry their voices into FOSIS's work, and help connect them to the training, resources, and support they need to serve their students well. Beyond ISoc engagement, you will be an active member of the Midlands team, contributing to events, campaigns, and projects that make a tangible difference to Muslim student life across the region.
This is not a passive role. It is for students who want to move beyond their own campus and play a part in the national Muslim student movement.
What You'll Be Doing

ISoc Engagement: Get to know the ISocs in your area. Understand their challenges, their wins, and what they need. Be the person committees call when they're looking for support, not just a name on a list.

Regional Projects & Events: Play an active role in planning and delivering Midlands initiatives. Lead or co-lead projects, support event logistics, and bring ideas for programmes and campaigns that serve students across the region.
Team Contribution: Show up for the Midlands team. Attend meetings, take ownership of your areas of work, and support FOSIS's wider regional and national priorities.

Student Leadership & Representation: Be an ambassador for what FOSIS stands for. Promote opportunities for Muslim students to get involved, and help build stronger connections between students, ISocs, and the wider movement.
What We're Looking For

Someone with a genuine passion for serving the Muslim student community. You do not need to have sat on an ISoc committee; you need initiative, reliability, and the drive to take ownership of work that matters. Strong communication, a collaborative spirit, and the creativity to make projects come alive.
What You'll Gain

Real leadership experience within a national organisation. The chance to lead projects, build relationships with student leaders across the Midlands and beyond, and develop skills in communications, project management, and event delivery, while doing work that is good for your deen.
This is a voluntary role designed to fit around your studies. You will be expected to actively contribute to Midlands projects and stay engaged with the team throughout the academic year.

roles.title: HR Operations & Recruitment Volunteer
description: Help build the team that powers FOSIS. In this role, you'll manage the full recruitment cycle, from advertising roles and screening applicants to coordinating interviews and onboarding new volunteers. You'll also maintain our HR systems and ensure every volunteer joins (and leaves) the organisation smoothly. If you have experience in HR or recruitment and want to put it to work for the Muslim student community, this one's for you.

roles.title: HR: Training & People Development Volunteer
description: Make sure every FOSIS volunteer feels supported, skilled, and set up to thrive. You'll coordinate training across the organisation, identify skills gaps, manage relationships with external providers, and lead on volunteer welfare and retention. This role suits someone with a people-first mindset who wants to build a culture of growth at a national Muslim student organisation.

roles.title: Graphic Designer: Media and Marketing
description: Design the Vision: Creative Lead & Graphic Designer

Make the Mission Unmissable. Can you turn a powerful message into a visual movement? We are looking for a high-caliber Graphic Designer to be the visual architect of FOSIS. Your work will be the face of a national organization, defining how the Muslim student community is seen and heard. We need a visual identity that inspires action and sets a new standard for professional excellence.
The Impact You’ll Have:
High-Impact Visuals: Design stunning posters and digital assets for national campaigns, major conferences, and community-wide initiatives.
Creative Quality Control: Act as the ultimate brand guardian, ensuring every piece of media, from Instagram carousels to print publications, meets a sharp and professional gold standard.
Strategic Brand Storytelling: Translate complex ideas into clean, accessible, and modern visual narratives that resonate across the UK and Ireland.
Unified Aesthetic: Lead the charge in maintaining a consistent and authentically Muslim brand identity that reflects our values and mission.
If you have the eye for detail and the heart for the Ummah, we want your portfolio.

roles.title: Mental Health Researcher
description: Muslim students are navigating mental health challenges that are often misunderstood, underserved, and shaped by experiences the mainstream sector rarely accounts for. Before FOSIS can build resources that genuinely help, we need to understand the landscape, what exists, what is missing, and what Muslim students actually need.
That is where you come in.

As a Mental Health Researcher, you will be the foundation of FOSIS's work in this space. Your research will directly shape the resources, partnerships, and guidance we develop for Muslim students across the country.
What You Will Be Doing

Research and Mapping: Identify and map mental health organisations, inclusivity bodies, and support services relevant to Muslim students in higher education. Help FOSIS build the partnerships that give students access to the right support.
Best Practice Review: Research existing standards across universities and specialist sectors to ensure everything FOSIS produces is evidence-based, high-quality, and practically useful.

Student Consultation: Engage directly with Muslim students, particularly those with lived experience including neurodivergent students and those with disabilities, to ensure our resources address real needs rather than assumed ones.
Compliance and Safeguarding: Ensure all research and drafted content aligns with safeguarding protocols and university standards.
Who We Are Looking For

Someone with genuine care for Muslim student wellbeing and the rigour to turn that care into credible, evidence-backed work. You may be studying psychology, social sciences, medicine, or a related field, or simply someone with strong research skills and a passion for this area. An understanding of the specific challenges facing Muslim students, including Islamophobia, identity, and cultural stigma around mental health, is a real asset.
What You Will Gain

Experience conducting research within a national advocacy organisation. The opportunity to contribute to resources that will reach Muslim students across the UK. And the knowledge that the work you do here genuinely matters.

roles.title: Fresher Pack Co-Ordinator
description: Every year, FOSIS distributes 10,000 Fresher Packs across 100+ ISOCs in the UK, and we need coordinators to deliver the project. As a Fresher Pack Coordinator, you’ll manage relationships with ISOCs, businesses and sponsors, coordinate logistics and allocations, work to real deadlines, and solve problems as they arise. It’s a defined, time-limited summer project that gives you practical experience in stakeholder management, operations, project delivery and commercial partnerships,while making a real national impact. We are looking for reliability, initiative and a willingness to learn.

roles.title: Project: Fresher Packs Team Member
description: Every September, Muslim students walk through university doors for the first time. They're navigating a new city, a new community, and often, for the first time, an identity as a Muslim adult in public life. Your job is to make sure FOSIS is there on day one.

We're looking for a Fresher Packs Coordinator to lead the end-to-end delivery of FOSIS's annual fresher packs - one of the most tangible, high-reach pieces of work our organisation produces. This isn't a passive role. You will touch every part of the process: what goes in the pack, who sponsors it, how it looks, and how it reaches ISoc committees across the country in time for Freshers' Week.
What You'll Own:

Curation & Content - Decide what goes in the pack. From survival guides and halal food directories to mental health resources and Islamic identity content, every insert should reflect FOSIS's four pillars and genuinely serve a Muslim fresher in week one of university life.

Sponsorship & Partnerships - Identify and pitch to brands, Islamic finance providers, halal food companies, and Muslim-owned businesses who want to reach 10,000 students. Manage agreements, deliverables, and relationships from brief to fulfilment.
Design & Production - Work with our design team to produce a pack that looks and feels like FOSIS: authoritative, warm, and distinctly Muslim. Oversee print production, packaging, and quality.

Logistics & Distribution - Coordinate nationwide delivery to ISoc committees across UK universities and colleges. Build the systems to track fulfilment, handle queries, and ensure no ISoc is left without their allocation.
ISoc Engagement - Brief ISoc committees on how to use and distribute the packs. The pack is only as powerful as the hands it reaches students through.
Why This Role Matters
The fresher pack is often a Muslim student's first encounter with the national Muslim student movement. Done well, it signals: you are not alone, there is a community here, and FOSIS is part of it.
If you are someone who thinks in systems, sweats the details, and cares deeply about Muslim students being set up to thrive, this role was built for you.

roles.title: Volunteer - North Sisters Education
description: There has never been a shortage of Muslimah students who want to learn. What has been missing is the infrastructure to connect them with qualified female scholars, credible Islamic knowledge, and learning communities that feel safe, serious, and built for them.
That is what North Sisters Education is building.

We are a project within FOSIS North creating a national ecosystem that gives Muslimah students real access to female sheikhas, ustadhaas, and scholars through webinars, halaqahs, a national speaker database, and leadership programmes. We are growing the team. If this work calls to you, we want you with us.
What We Are Building

A national database of verified female Islamic speakers accessible to ISocs and chaplaincies across the country. A credibility framework so students know the knowledge they are receiving is sound. Direct access points including online circles and termly scholar sessions. Leadership training to develop the next generation of Muslimah student leaders. And partnerships with institutions like Zad Academy and the Maryam Institute to open doors to structured Islamic education for Muslim students.
Where We Need Help
Research and Outreach: Interviewing Muslimah students to map barriers and needs. Identifying scholars, organisations, and institutions to partner with.
Framework Development: Helping build the speaker credibility and vetting process that underpins the project.
Content and Communications: Creating promotional materials and social media content that speaks to our audience.
Events and Programme Coordination: Supporting the delivery of webinars, scholar sessions, workshops, and our annual Female Scholars Conference.
Leadership Development: Contributing to halaqah leadership training for Muslimah student leaders.
Who We Are Looking For

A Muslimah student or recent graduate who believes access to authentic Islamic knowledge should not depend on where you study or who you happen to know on campus. You are reliable, collaborative, and ready to own a piece of work that outlasts your time at university. Previous ISoc experience is welcomed but not essential.

roles.title: General Officer
description: • Shall support the Palestine Team in delivering its campaigns, projects and initiatives, contributing to areas of work according to their skills, interests and capacity.
• Shall assist other members of the team with research, campaigning, communications, events, outreach and other activities as required.
• Shall contribute to the development and implementation of initiatives supporting Palestinian advocacy and Gazan students.
• Shall attend and actively contribute to team meetings, discussions and activities.
• Shall undertake additional tasks and responsibilities as reasonably required by the Chair or relevant lead, according to their capacity and availability.

roles.title: Research & Policy Officer
description: • Shall monitor relevant university policies, sector developments, research and emerging opportunities relating to Palestinian advocacy, university divestment and the rights and welfare of Palestinian students.
• Shall gather, analyse and summarise relevant research, policy developments, financial information and briefings to inform the team's campaigns and policy positions.
• Shall identify opportunities for advocacy and campaign engagement arising from developments within the higher education sector.
• Shall support the development of evidence-based campaign strategies, awareness initiatives and policy proposals.
• Shall work with relevant partners and student organisations to facilitate collaborative research and advocacy initiatives.

roles.title: External Partnerships & Relations Officer
description: • Shall develop and maintain relationships with Islamic Societies, Palestine-focused student organisations, businesses, community organisations and other relevant external partners.
• Shall identify opportunities for collaboration, joint initiatives and partnerships to strengthen the reach and impact of the team's work.
• Shall identify and approach potential sponsors, businesses and external partners to secure financial, in-kind and other forms of support.
• Shall coordinate collaborative initiatives across universities and student organisations to build wider support for Palestinian advocacy.
• Shall maintain effective communication with external partners and ensure relationships are developed and sustained professionally.

roles.title: Divestment Lead
description: • Shall lead the development and coordination of targeted student-led campaigns calling on UK universities to adopt ethical investment policies and divest from companies and institutions complicit in mass atrocities, genocide and occupation.
• Shall research university investments, endowments, financial structures, procurement and relevant contracts to identify opportunities and leverage points for divestment.
• Shall develop campaign strategies, policy proposals and advocacy materials to support university divestment campaigns.
• Shall work with Islamic Societies, student organisations, academics and wider coalitions to coordinate and strengthen divestment campaigns.
• Shall support student groups in organising petitions, meetings, campaigns and other forms of advocacy to advance divestment objectives.

Preferred Experience: Student leadership experience, such as a Sabbatical Officer or senior Student Union role, with an understanding of university governance, committee structures and student campaigning.

roles.title: Gazan Scholars Lead
description: • Shall oversee and coordinate projects and initiatives supporting Palestinian scholars and Gazan students before, during and after their studies in the UK.
• Shall work with universities, Islamic Societies, external organisations and relevant stakeholders to develop academic, practical and institutional support pathways.
• Shall coordinate initiatives aimed at facilitating access to education, academic support, guidance and integration for Gazan scholars.
• Shall monitor the effectiveness of scholar support initiatives and identify areas for improvement or further intervention.
• Shall ensure initiatives supporting Gazan scholars are aligned with the wider objectives of the Palestine Team and FOSIS's student welfare work.

roles.title: Gazan Scholars Welfare Officer
description: • Shall work directly with Gazan students and local Islamic Society welfare representatives to identify their welfare, academic and practical support needs.
• Shall help connect Gazan students with appropriate university, Islamic Society, community and other support services.
• Shall work with relevant stakeholders to establish clear and accessible pathways for students seeking support.
• Shall maintain regular communication with Gazan students and welfare representatives to identify emerging issues and ensure appropriate support is available.
• Shall contribute to initiatives aimed at improving the welfare, inclusion and sense of community of Gazan students throughout their academic journey in the UK.
